paragraphs: The CLS 500 was a V8-powered mainstay of the original CLS range, spanning two generations from 2004 to 2018. The first-generation C219 (2004-2010) uses the M273 - a 5.5-litre naturally aspirated V8. The second-generation C218 (2010-2018) switched to the M278, a 4.7-litre twin-turbo V8 - a genuinely different engine with a different character and layout. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components and rebuild specifics differ between them - which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every CLS 500 on the road.

compatibility.intro: Because the CLS 500 spans two distinct V8 engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement - or assuming an M273 part will work on an M278 car - risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic CLS quote - it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
